result.topic_en: Euler discusses determining the friction coefficient α from the width of capillary tubes that just stop pouring out water, how this depends on atmospheric pressure (so in a vacuum such tubes would empty except for capillary retention), and argues that atmospheric pressure, through friction, always retards efflux, suggesting this explains the observed acceleration of efflux by electricity.

360 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

nes $gg$ ſint diuerſae, iique aqua repleantur; tum ex ampliori­bus quidem aqua effluet, ex arctioribus vero ſecus; tantum igitur opus eſt, vt eius tubuli, qui aquam non amplius eiicit, amplitudo $gg$ menſuretur, eritque tum $\alpha = \frac{g}{l}$. Hic autem effluxus verus ſpectari debet, quo aqua continuo tractu effluit; ſi enim guttatim tantum decidit, idem erit, ac ſi aqua non effluere­t. Cum enim frictio demum in vero motu cernatur, quamdiu aqua quieſcit, ob grauitatem guttae ſenſim auellentur ac decident, id quod frictio impedire non valet.

60. Patet ergo gracilitatem huiusmodi tubulorum, qui aquam contentam, etiamſi vtrinque ſint aperti, non effluere ſinunt, a pondere atmoſphaerae $l$ pendere, quoniam hoc euenit, ſi $g < \alpha l$. Hinc videmus, in vacuo, vbi $l = 0$, iſtos tubulos aquam omnino effundere, niſi quatenus, ob naturam, quae tubulis capillaribus propria eſt, aqua in iis ad certam altitudinem retineatur, reliqua autem aqua effluet in vacuo, quae in aere guttatim tantum decidebat.

61. Generatim autem intelligitur, ob preſſionem atmoſphaerae effluxum aquae ſemper retardari, et quidem frictionem huius retardationis eſſe cauſam: vidimus enim (54), quo minor ſit preſſio atmoſphaerae $l$, eo maiori celeritate aquam exilire. Quodſi ergo a cauſa quacunque preſſio atmoſphaerae imminuatur, aqua velocius ex vaſe effluet; quam propterea cauſam eſſe exiſtimo, quod ab electricitate effluxus aquae accelerari obſeruetur.

items.quote: tantum igitur opus eſt, vt eius tubuli, qui aquam non amplius eiicit, amplitudo $gg$ menſuretur, eritque tum $\alpha = \frac{g}{l}$.
items.english: So one need only measure the width gg of the tube which no longer ejects water, and then α = g/l.

items.quote: Hinc videmus, in vacuo, vbi $l = 0$, iſtos tubulos aquam omnino effundere, niſi quatenus, ob naturam, quae tubulis capillaribus propria eſt, aqua in iis ad certam altitudinem retineatur
items.english: Hence we see that in a vacuum, where l = 0, these tubes pour out the water entirely, except insofar as, by the nature proper to capillary tubes, water is retained in them to a certain height.

items.quote: quam propterea cauſam eſſe exiſtimo, quod ab electricitate effluxus aquae accelerari obſeruetur.
items.english: I therefore judge this to be the cause why the efflux of water is observed to be accelerated by electricity.
